newsitem.title: USA: TWA sees Q3 results below year-ago level.
newsitem.headline: TWA sees Q3 results below year-ago level.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said it expects pre-tax results for its third quarter to be below year-ago levels due in part to "a short-term loss of premium fare international bookings following the loss of Flight 800 on July 17."
Summer traffic, load factors and overall revenues this year exceeded 1995 levels, but TWA said July and August yields were below year-ago levels.
The airline also noted "significant cost increases in July and August relative to the prior year."

Immediately following the tragic crash of TWA Flight 800 into the Atlantic Ocean off Long Island, New York, the airline said it noted "a slight temporary fall-off in advance bookings ... (resulting) in September passenger loads that are below expectations." No adverse impact on advance bookings for October and later has been observed, TWA said.

The airline said it "experienced an unusually high level of domestic flight cancellations in July and August partly as a result of an extremely aggressive growth plan for summer flying" that led to higher costs and revenue losses.
In addition, the airline said it has been hurt by an industry-wide fuel price increase that has hit harder at TWA because of its less fuel-efficient fleet.

"Operationally and emotionally, this has been an extremely difficult summer for the people of TWA, and unfortunately it now appears that we will see these difficulties reflected in third quarter results," said chief executive Jeffrey Erickson.
Separately, TWA announced discounts of up to 55 percent off 21-day advance purchase structural fares for domestic flights with some restrictions, matching similar cuts by AMR Corp's Airlines.
